_note: Films and series for /cultura/films-and-series: title, year, maker and our own short description, nothing else. No streaming links (they change). `level` is our estimate of how much Italian you need to enjoy it with Italian subtitles. Years and makers are from memory of well-documented works and are all listed 'to verify' in tmp-culture/zitate-filme-kalender.verify.md. Group `mondo` holds Italian-language films about Italians on the move and about arrivals in Italy (no Swiss production included because none could be named with certainty). Added 2026-11-15.

items.title: Il postino
items.text: On a small island in the 1950s, a young postman gets to know the exiled poet Pablo Neruda. Slow, gentle and full of simple, clear Italian.

items.title: La vita è bella
items.text: A father uses humour to protect his small son in a very dark time. The first half is a light comedy, the second half is serious.

items.title: Nuovo Cinema Paradiso
items.text: A film director remembers the village cinema of his childhood in Sicily and the projectionist who taught him about films and life.

items.title: Perfetti sconosciuti
items.text: Friends at a dinner agree to put their phones on the table and read every message aloud. Almost all of it happens in one room, so the dialogue is easy to follow.

items.title: Le fate ignoranti
items.text: A woman in Rome finds out after her husband's death that he had a secret life, and she meets the people around him. Everyday Italian and a warm story about family you choose.

items.title: La grande bellezza
items.text: An ageing writer walks through the parties and the old streets of Rome. A rich, slow and very beautiful film that won an Oscar for the best foreign film.

items.title: Pane e tulipani
items.text: A housewife is left behind on a coach trip and decides to stay in Venice. A light comedy with clear speech, good for a first film in Italian.

items.title: Mediterraneo
items.text: In 1941 a small group of Italian soldiers is sent to a quiet Greek island and slowly forgets the war. A gentle comedy that won an Oscar for the best foreign film.

items.title: L'amica geniale
items.by: RAI and HBO, from the novels by Elena Ferrante
items.text: Two girls grow up in a poor district of Naples in the 1950s and stay friends for life. Some of the speech is Neapolitan dialect, so subtitles help.

items.title: Mare fuori
items.text: Young people in a juvenile prison in Naples. A very popular series with fast, modern speech and a lot of Neapolitan, so it is a challenge even for advanced learners.

items.title: Il cammino della speranza
items.text: Sicilian miners who have lost their work try to reach France on foot and by lorry. An early, serious film about leaving home to find work.

items.title: Pane e cioccolata
items.text: An Italian worker looks for a better life in Switzerland and finds a lonely, difficult life among other immigrants. Funny and sad at the same time.

items.title: Lamerica
items.text: Two Italian con men go to Albania after the fall of communism to make money, and meet a man who shows them what leaving home means. It echoes Italy's own history of emigration.

items.title: Nuovomondo
items.text: A Sicilian family sails to America in the early 1900s and waits at Ellis Island. Simple speech, with some Sicilian, and strong images.

items.title: Io sono Li
items.text: A Chinese woman works in a bar in Chioggia, near Venice, and becomes friends with an older fisherman. A quiet film about arrival and belonging in Italy today.
